intent_signal: Procedural/transactional 'how-to' intent: the searcher is ready to apply and wants the exact portal, steps, fees, documents and timeline. SERP is dominated by law-firm service pages (Siam Legal, Fragomen) and independent step-by-step guides, signaling Google rewards both authoritative source credibility AND a concrete, complete application walkthrough. Activity-specific qualifiers (Muay Thai) already surface in the top independent guides.
common_ground: Official application portal: Thailand e-Visa at https://www.thaievisa.go.th (must apply from OUTSIDE Thailand; cannot apply from inside the country)
Application fee: 10,000 THB (~$275-$300 / commonly cited ~$290 USD), non-refundable even if rejected
Financial proof: at least 500,000 THB (~$14,000-$16,000 USD) bank balance, OR equivalent income ~50,000 THB/month (~$1,400) / employment-salary evidence
Minimum age: 20 years old at time of application
Visa validity: 5 years, multiple entry, up to 180 days per stay, extendable once by 180 days for 1,900 THB
Processing time: 5-15 business days officially (most sources); in practice up to ~3-6 weeks / 30 business days in peak season

Core documents: passport (6+ months validity, blank pages), passport photo (4x6 cm), completed application form, proof of accommodation, flight itinerary, bank statements (3-6 months), and activity/qualifying-activity evidence
Health insurance: $50,000 USD minimum medical coverage covering Thailand (required by some embassies, strongly recommended generally)

Generic application steps: create e-Visa account -> select DTV -> choose category/activity -> select embassy of residence -> upload PDF/JPEG documents -> pay fee online -> wait for processing -> receive approval email -> enter Thailand
Qualifying categories: Workcation (remote work/digital nomad), Thai Soft Power (Muay Thai training, cooking courses, wellness/medical, sports, seminars), and Dependent (spouse + children under 20)
Muay Thai is an explicitly recognized Soft Power qualifying activity; required docs = letter/enrollment confirmation from a registered Muay Thai camp + payment receipt + training schedule
Post-arrival obligations: 90-day reporting (tm47.immigration.go.th), TM30 address registration
Key restriction: cannot work for Thai companies or earn income from Thai clients; no Thai work permit is issued

gap.description: Every ranking page describes the process abstractly but NONE provide: (1) annotated real screenshots of the thaievisa.go.th portal flow, (2) a lived, first-person walkthrough with what immigration actually scrutinizes and how long each step really took, or (3) an interactive/downloadable document checklist. Critically, the Soft Power / Muay Thai route is under-served: law-firm pages (Siam Legal, Fragomen) barely mention it and give no camp-document specifics, while the independent guides mention 'gym letter + payment receipt' in one line without showing what an acceptable camp enrollment letter looks like or how a camp prepares it for you. No competitor positions a Muay Thai camp as a first-party document provider that de-risks the application.

weakness: Top law-firm results (Fragomen, Siam Legal) omit hard facts the searcher wants right now: no portal URL, no 10,000 THB fee, no processing-time figures on Fragomen
No competitor shows real portal screenshots or a step-by-step visual walkthrough

Gaps on what immigration actually checks/rejects, apostille/authentication, and post-approval balance maintenance
